primary_unit_types: Process furnaces/heaters; Steam boilers; CHP steam turbines; Gas turbines + HRSG; Fired reboilers
end_use_split: Direct process heat ~55%; Steam/boiler ~25%; CHP heat fraction ~20%
epsilon_source: Saad et al. 2026 (furnace 75%, boiler 88-94%, CHP 40%); LCP BREF 2017; Refinery BREF 2015
notes: OtherGas = refinery fuel gas (still gas, H2, C1-C2) burned on-site; all combustion = heat. Weighted epsilon across furnaces, boilers, CHP. No eta adjustment needed - LCP reports combustion fuel only.

primary_unit_types: Coke oven batteries; Under-firing burners; By-product recovery boilers
notes: OtherGas = coke oven gas (COG) used as under-firing fuel. High-temp direct heat ~1000-1100 degC. Lower epsilon due to high exhaust losses. No eta adjustment needed.

primary_unit_types: Blast furnace stoves; Hot blast stoves; Reheating furnaces; Sinter plants; CHP boilers (BFG-fired); Ladle preheaters
end_use_split: Direct process heat ~65%; CHP heat fraction ~20%; Steam ~15%
epsilon_source: Iron & Steel BREF 2012; Saad et al. 2026 (direct process 75%); Fraunhofer ISI 2024
notes: OtherGas = blast furnace gas (BFG) + COG - byproducts burned for heat. No blast furnace coke in LCP fuel columns so no reducing agent adjustment needed. Dominant process is high-temp direct heat >1000 degC.

primary_unit_types: Smelting furnaces; Reverberatory furnaces; Roasters; Anode furnaces; Steam boilers
epsilon_source: Non-ferrous Metals BREF 2017; Saad et al. 2026
notes: High-temp direct process heat 800-1200 degC. Nearly all CO2 from combustion. Secondary Al uses rotary furnaces (fuel-fired); primary Al uses EAF (electricity-dominated, unlikely in LCP set).

primary_unit_types: Rotary kilns; Precalciners; Cyclone preheater towers; Raw meal dryers
epsilon_source: Saad et al. 2026; EU Cement BREF 2013; Liu et al. 2015 J.Energy Inst.
notes: LCP fuel = combustion fuel only. Calcination CO2 (CaCO3->CaO+CO2) is a process emission not tied to fuel consumption - does not appear in LCP fuel columns. No eta adjustment needed. Kiln temps >1400 degC.

primary_unit_types: Shaft kilns (PFR); Rotary kilns; Parallel-flow regenerative kilns
epsilon_source: Lime BREF 2013; Cement & Lime BREF revision 2019
notes: Same reasoning as cement - calcination CO2 not in LCP fuel columns. No eta needed. PFR shaft kilns most efficient in EU. Kiln temps 900-1200 degC.

primary_unit_types: End-fired regenerative furnaces; Cross-fired furnaces; Oxy-fuel furnaces; Electric boosters; Lehrs (annealing)
epsilon_source: Glass BREF 2012; Agora Industry / Fraunhofer ISI 2024
notes: Low epsilon because melting at 1400-1600 degC has large exhaust losses; regenerative furnaces recover heat through checkerwork but net efficiency still 45-55%. OtherGas may be producer gas. No eta adjustment needed.

primary_unit_types: Tank furnaces; Cupola furnaces (stone wool); Curing ovens
epsilon_source: Mineral Wool BREF 2001 (under revision); Glass BREF 2012
notes: Melting at 1400-1550 degC. Similar reasoning to glass sector. No eta adjustment needed.

primary_unit_types: Steam crackers; Process furnaces; CHP steam turbines; Industrial boilers; Fired reboilers
end_use_split: Direct furnaces ~45%; Steam/boiler ~30%; CHP heat fraction ~25%
epsilon_range_by_unit: Furnace 0.75-0.80; Gas boiler 0.88-0.92; CHP heat 0.40; weighted avg ~0.80
epsilon_source: Saad et al. 2026; Chemicals BREF 2017; Fraunhofer ISI 2024
notes: OtherGas = tail gas, syn gas, refinery gas - all combusted for heat. CHP very common in large chemical complexes. No eta adjustment for general petrochemicals. H2 plants require separate treatment - see row below.

primary_unit_types: Steam methane reformers; Reformer furnaces; Shift reactors
end_use_split: Reformer furnace heat ~100% of reported fuel
epsilon_source: Saad et al. 2026; EPA GHGRP Chemicals Sector Profile
notes: IMPORTANT: methane used as feedstock in SMR reaction (CH4+H2O->CO+H2) is NOT combustion fuel and does NOT appear in LCP fuel columns. LCP reports only fuel burned in reformer burners to heat the reaction. So epsilon applies normally to reported LCP fuel. No eta adjustment needed. Identify H2 plants by facility name if possible.

primary_unit_types: Steam boilers; CHP units; Process furnaces; Granulation dryers; Reformers (NH3)
notes: NH3 feedstock gas does not appear in LCP fuel columns (same logic as H2). Reported fuel = combustion for heat. No eta adjustment needed. Apply standard boiler/furnace epsilon to reported LCP fuel.

primary_unit_types: Moving grate incinerators; Waste-to-energy boilers; Steam turbines (CHP); Auxiliary gas/coal burners
epsilon_range_by_unit: Gas auxiliary boiler 0.88-0.92; Coal auxiliary boiler 0.83-0.88; weighted ~0.85
epsilon_source: Waste Incineration BREF 2019; EU IED Art. 50
notes: IMPORTANT DISTINCTION: fuel in LCP columns (gas, coal) is AUXILIARY burner fuel only - used to maintain >850 degC per EU Waste Incineration Directive. Main energy source is waste itself (not in LCP fuel columns). Apply epsilon to reported fuel as standard boiler combustion. No eta adjustment.

primary_unit_types: Rotary kiln incinerators; High-temp afterburners; Waste-fired boilers; Secondary combustion chambers
end_use_split: Direct kiln combustion ~70%; Heat recovery boiler ~30%
notes: Same auxiliary fuel logic as 5(b). Reported LCP fuel = auxiliary combustion to maintain temperature. Apply epsilon as combustion for heat. No eta adjustment.

primary_unit_types: Recovery boilers (black liquor); Bark/biomass boilers; CHP back-pressure turbines; Lime kilns; Paper machine dryers
end_use_split: Steam boilers ~50%; CHP heat fraction ~40%; Direct (lime kiln) ~10%
epsilon_range_by_unit: Recovery boiler 0.65-0.72; Bark/biomass boiler 0.80-0.85; Gas boiler 0.88-0.92; CHP heat 0.40; weighted avg ~0.82
epsilon_source: Pulp & Paper BREF 2015; Fraunhofer ISI 2016 Mapping EU Heat; Saad et al. 2026
notes: Recovery boiler has lower epsilon because it also recovers pulping chemicals (complex process). All combustion = heat. CHP near-universal in Scandinavian integrated mills. OtherSolidFuels = bark, wood waste, sludge. No eta adjustment.

primary_unit_types: Wood waste/biomass boilers; Thermal oil heaters; Direct-fired dryers; Hot press platens (steam); CHP units
end_use_split: Steam/thermal oil ~45%; Direct dryers ~35%; CHP heat ~20%
epsilon_range_by_unit: Biomass boiler 0.80-0.85; Gas boiler 0.88; Direct dryer 0.72-0.78; weighted ~0.80
epsilon_source: Wood-Based Panels BREF 2015; Saad et al. 2026
notes: All combustion = heat. Wood-based panels need high-temp drying 150-200 degC and hot pressing. OtherSolidFuels = wood waste from production. No eta adjustment.

primary_unit_types: High-pressure steam boilers; Multi-effect evaporators; CHP back-pressure turbines; Juice heaters; Vacuum pans; Pulp dryers
end_use_split: Steam boiler ~50%; CHP heat fraction ~40%; Direct drying ~10%
epsilon_range_by_unit: Gas boiler 0.88-0.92; CHP heat 0.40; weighted avg ~0.85
notes: All combustion = heat. Sugar processing is highly steam-intensive (100-130 degC multi-effect evaporation). CHP back-pressure turbines near-universal in EU beet sugar plants. Fully consistent with Eichenlaub flat 85% assumption. No eta adjustment.

primary_unit_types: Steam boilers; Pasteurisation systems; Spray dryers; Evaporators; CHP (larger plants)
notes: All combustion = heat. Low-temp steam processes 70-150 degC. Spray drying ~200 degC. Standard gas boiler epsilon applies. Eichenlaub 85% flat assumption fully appropriate here. No eta adjustment.

primary_unit_types: Steam boilers; Hot water systems; Drying chambers
notes: Tiny sample. Low-temp processes <150 degC. All gas = heat. Standard gas boiler epsilon applies directly. No eta adjustment.
